summary:
CONFIRMED UNAUTHORIZED ACCESS on web-01 through the shared deploy account's password.

What happened: 64.227.126.70 (a cloud host, not a staff address) logged in to web-01 as the shared 'deploy' account using its password about five times a day from 29 Oct 2026 until my containment at about 19:04 UTC on 12 Nov (about 76 successful password logins in the 14 days of logs; 4 of them today). Deploy is the CI account, which should only log in with its key from ci-01. Deploy had NOPASSWD sudo to larkspur-deploy, larkspur-restart and rsync. rsync as root is a root shell, so this was a path to full root. The logs show no sudo use by this IP beyond the normal CI release command, so I cannot prove root was obtained, but I treated it as possible. The attacker had read access to deploy-owned files including wp-config.php. The same IP appears nowhere on db-01 or ci-01.

Not a compromise (checked): 98.212.187.236 is the editor Lucia's home login to WordPress; wlin, mfischer, dana, jcole, pshah and hgrant logins are from their known keys or home IPs; ci-01 release and db-01 dump traffic is the normal key-based traffic. The three invoice adjustments by the bookkeeper (invoices 12, 14, 25) each match their shop order total exactly and are logged, so they look legitimate, but please confirm.

Contained / changed:
- Blocked 64.227.126.70 on web-01 with iptables (not persistent across reboot; please keep it or add it to the firewall config).
- deploy account is now key-only (sshd Match User deploy: PasswordAuthentication no). Verified: the CI key login still works and the 3-minute release runs (last ok 19:06).
- Removed deploy's NOPASSWD rsync sudo rule (the offsite job uses root's own rsync, not this rule). Backup of the old sudoers file in /root.
- Rotated deploy-password (the old one stops working; Maria and old scripts must use the new value from the staff vault/help desk; Maria should use her own key, not deploy), app-db-password (wp-config.php is owned by deploy and was readable by the compromised account; the site is up, HTTP 200), and payment-key (root-only copies were reachable through the rsync sudo path; payouts check still OK). The second copy of the live key in /etc/larkspur/gateway.env on db-01 (used by larkspur-settle) was updated to the new key; settle ok.
- web-01 account 'jpark' (contractor Jun Park) is NOT in the staff directory, was in the sudo group, had never logged in and was being brute-forced. Removed from sudo and locked on web-01; locked on ci-01. If Jun Park should have access, Maria should decide and add them to the directory.
- Grafana (port 3000) and the node exporter (port 9100) were listening on the public address. Bound both to the office address 10.20.0.10 (reachable over the office VPN only). Verified listeners.
- MariaDB on db-01 was bound to 0.0.0.0; set to 10.20.0.20. Restarted briefly; verified web-01 DB access, dump job and settle job.

Not changed / for Maria:
- Root-only secrets not rotated because I have no log evidence they were read: grafana-s3-key, smtp-password, backup-password (restic), web-01 and db-01 root secrets, billing_app DB password. Consider rotating them; the root path is now closed.
- Offsite upload from db-01/ci-01 to the Wasabi bucket has failed with 'no route' since at least 15:41 today (12 archives waiting). Local dumps are fine; the offsite path needs a fix.
- Password SSH logins are open to the whole internet for all staff on web-01 (many brute-force attempts; no success found except the deploy case). Recommend moving staff to keys and adding fail2ban. I did not do this now because several staff log in with passwords from home and would be locked out.
- An unreleased file, plugin inc/booking.php (Theo's April copy), sits untracked and publicly reachable on web-01. It contains no malicious code and nothing references it, but it should be committed or removed.
- Mention of 24.30.29.136 (jcole, pshah, hgrant password logins): a shared home IP, not flagged.

Update after the first report. Containment verified at about 19:08 UTC: 64.227.126.70 is still blocked on web-01; the deploy account refuses password logins (sshd -T confirmed); the CI release is running (last ok 19:06); the site returns HTTP 200; payouts and settlement are ok; the database dump ran at 19:00.

Since containment, the only deploy login attempts are failed password attempts from other internet addresses (34.86.129.55, 80.94.220.51, 54.36.223.14, 185.224.134.211, 138.68.139.53). None succeeded. These are brute-force attempts that the key-only setting now blocks, so I did not block those addresses. Logins on db-01 and ci-01 are normal (known keys and home IPs). No new compromise found on db-01 or ci-01.

Open items are unchanged from the first report: root-only secrets not rotated for lack of evidence of reading; offsite upload failing since 15:41; password SSH for staff still open to the internet; three bookkeeper invoice adjustments to confirm; the jpark account needs a decision from Maria; the iptables block is not persistent across reboots.

Final update. The intrusion via the deploy password from 64.227.126.70 on web-01 is contained. Changes since the last update: the IP block on web-01 is now re-applied at boot by /usr/local/sbin/larkspur-blocklist, called from /etc/rc.local, because this host does not run systemd. The block is active now. Checks at 19:09 UTC on all three servers show only normal activity: the release (last ok 19:09), maintenance, the site (HTTP 200), payouts and settlement (ok), and the database dump (19:00). Deploy refuses passwords (sshd -T confirmed). Failed root and deploy password attempts on web-01 come from internet scanners and do not succeed. Open items for Maria are unchanged from the earlier reports: root-only secrets not rotated for lack of evidence of reading; offsite upload failing since 15:41; password SSH for staff still open to the internet; three bookkeeper invoice adjustments to confirm; the jpark decision; and the attacker IP block should be made permanent in the firewall config when convenient.
